new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Boursin Garlic & Fine Herbs is a branded Gournay cheese sold in 5.2 oz foil pucks at roughly $4.50-6.00 each (about $15/lb), against cream cheese at roughly $4/lb - not the same price class, and it is a spreadable cultured-cream cheese, not ricotta, provolone or parmesan (the only near vocabulary rows). The pre-resolver reports board ABSENT with no commodity and no capture match, so nothing prices this food under another spelling. If an existing id covers herbed cream-cheese spread, alias to it; otherwise this line is a real recurring ingredient and needs its own id, because pantry-static pricing on 12 oz of a $5 cheese would materially misprice the recipe.

registrar_rulings.reason: The food is genuinely unpriced: zero hits for boursin/gournay/spread in all three id namespaces, the alias map, the dupe allowlist, and the live feed's product names (per-file re-sweep, not the batch grep). Nearest priced row is cream-cheese at $0.13/oz vs ~$0.87-1.15/oz for gournay pucks - a 6-9x gap and a different cultured/herbed product, so alias would silently misprice; but 'boursin' is a BRAND and brands never become ids, so mint the generic class id garlic-herb-cheese-spread in the recipe-only namespace (recipe-board-everyday baseline + recipe-commodities.json), with includes covering boursin|gournay|garlic\s*(?:&|and)?\s*(?:fine\s+)?herbs?\s+(?:cheese\s+spread|spreadable\s+cheese|gournay), excludes at neighboring-commodity rigor (crackers, dip, queso, cream cheese, pub cheese, veggie/chive cream cheese tubs, snack packs), an allowlist pair garlic-herb-cheese-spread<->cream-cheese ('same food family, different form/price class: cultured herbed gournay vs plain cream cheese'), and a recipe-floor-id-map entry boursin-cheese -> garlic-herb-cheese-spread so the recipe spelling resolves; separately the ingredient NAME needs its own vocabulary row (nearest rows ricotta/provolone/parmesan are different foods) with fdc:169081 'Cheese spread, cream cheese base' as a plausible macro source pending label confirmation - the name ruling does not mint the id and vice versa.

macro_cross_check: Done by hand over all 13 lines at source scale, 6 servings. Ours 620 cal / 52.0 protein / 55.5 carbs / 20.2 fat per serving vs source 503 / 49 / 52. PROTEIN agrees within 6%, which is the instrument that points at portions, and carbs within 7% - so no portion is wrong. Calories are 23% high, and the source's own arithmetic explains it: 49 P + 52 C accounts for 404 of its 503 cal, leaving only 11 g of fat per serving, which is impossible for a dish carrying a whole Boursin puck (56 g fat), 112 g parmesan and 1 lb of cottage cheese. Our 20.2 g fat is the defensible figure. 620 cal sits inside the 450-800 band, so the recipe stands.
